items.why: The report states "Both spectra are graphene" and gives G at 1580.4 and 2D at 2680.9 cm-1 on Au, and G at 1581.0 and 2D at 2695.6 cm-1 on Cu.

It gives D at 1344 cm-1 on Au and 1349.6 cm-1 on Cu, with "Au ... ID/IG about 0.97 (heights); Cu ... ID/IG about 0.62 +/- 0.27", and flags the Cu value as poorly constrained ("about 1.3 sigma, so it is not established").

The report puts the difference down to "metal-specific graphene-metal coupling" and to possible carbon precipitation on cooling; it never offers strain from rapid solidification as the authors' explanation for the stronger D on Au.

It treats ID/IG as a defect level and says strain is "Not separable" without a reference, noting the G shift does not resolve whether the 2D upshift is strain. It never says outright that D needs defects or edges to appear, or that a strain explanation for D should be checked against the G and 2D positions.

It asks "What laser wavelength was used? It sets the D and 2D reference positions, the L_D relation..." and notes in the caveats that D and 2D disperse with excitation energy; its L_D relation uses lambda^4.

It notes "The Cu spectrum is near the detection limit: G height about 3 times the point noise, D about 2.6 sigma", gives error bars on the Cu ratios, and points out that both spectra are single acquisitions with no repeat.

wrong_claims.why: Although the summary says no defect distance can be stated, the properties list "L_D about 11 nm (514 nm), 12 nm (532 nm), 17 nm (633 nm) for Au, conditional on the laser wavelength", which are quantitative L_D values given without a known wavelength.
The report never says the D peak on Au is caused by strain; it brings in strain only for the 2D width and the Cu 2D shift, and only as possibilities.
